stem: A 70-year-old woman has painful swallowing and burning behind the breastbone that began 3 weeks after she started a weekly tablet for osteoporosis. She takes it with a sip of water just before lying back down in bed. Endoscopy shows several erosions in the lower esophagus.
oneliner: 70F + new weekly tablet for osteoporosis + taken with a sip of water, then lies down + 3 wk later odynophagia + lower esophageal erosions → which drug?
ask: Which medication most likely caused this?

whyNot.A: **SERM**: risk is clots and hot flashes, not esophageal injury
whyNot.E: **Injection every 6 months**: no pill to stick in the esophagus

why: **Weekly osteoporosis tablet + little water + lying down → esophageal erosions** = pill esophagitis from a **bisphosphonate**. Take it upright with a full glass of water.

drug.name: Alendronate
drug.how: Binds bone hydroxyapatite and makes osteoclasts undergo apoptosis
drug.use: Osteoporosis, Paget disease, hypercalcemia of malignancy (IV forms)
drug.watch: Pill esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femur fractures

stem: A 58-year-old man with recurrent gout and a low 24-hour urinary uric acid excretion starts probenecid. Three weeks later he has sudden colicky left flank pain with hematuria. A plain abdominal film shows no stone shadow. He has no fever or rash, his creatinine and potassium are normal, and his urine volume is unchanged. He drinks little water.
oneliner: 58M + recurrent gout, low urinary uric acid + probenecid started + 3 wk later colicky flank pain, hematuria + no stone on plain film + normal creatinine and K → which drug effect?
ask: Which of the following drug effects most likely explains these symptoms?

options.A: Bladder mucosal injury from a toxic metabolite
options.B: Immune-mediated injury of the renal interstitium
options.C: Loss of collecting duct responsiveness to ADH

whyNot.A: Seen with **cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide** (acrolein); he takes neither, and his pain is **flank colic**
whyNot.B: Interstitial nephritis brings **fever, rash and rising creatinine**; he has **none**
whyNot.C: Causes **polyuria and dilute urine**; his **urine volume is unchanged**
whyNot.D: Would raise **potassium**, which is **normal**, and does not cause colic

answer: Uric acid stone from increased urinary uric acid
why: **Probenecid blocks urate reabsorption in the proximal tubule**, so more uric acid enters the urine. In a man who drinks little, that uric acid can precipitate as a **radiolucent uric acid stone** (colic, hematuria, nothing on plain film). Fluids and urine alkalinization reduce the risk.

drug.name: Probenecid
drug.how: Inhibits urate reabsorption (URAT1) and organic anion secretion in the proximal tubule, so more urate is excreted
drug.use: Gout from urate underexcretion; prolongs penicillin levels
drug.watch: Uric acid stones, initial gout flare, GI upset, rash; not for acute attacks or uric acid overproducers; aspirin blunts its effect

idea.rule: Uricosuric drugs move uric acid into the urine, so they can make uric acid stones.
also: Avoid uricosurics in uric acid overproducers and in stone formers; use allopurinol
Keep patients hydrated and alkalinize the urine when starting a uricosuric
Allopurinol lowers production and does not raise urinary uric acid
Aspirin in low doses blunts the uricosuric effect

stem: A 64-year-old man has had three gout attacks in the last year. Since a coronary stent was placed 14 months ago, he has taken aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin, clopidogrel, amlodipine and losartan. His serum urate has risen from 7.4 to 9.1 mg/dL over this period, and renal function is normal.
oneliner: 64M + recurrent gout + since coronary stent on aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin, clopidogrel, amlodipine, losartan + urate rising to 9.1 → which drug is raising urate?
ask: Which of his medications is most likely contributing to the rising urate?

whyNot.A: An angiotensin receptor blocker that is mildly **uricosuric**, so it tends to lower urate
whyNot.B: Statins have **little effect** on urate and do not cause gout
whyNot.D: A P2Y12 blocker with **no recognised effect** on urate handling
whyNot.E: A calcium channel blocker with **no meaningful effect** on urate

why: **Low-dose aspirin** competes for tubular secretion and **reduces renal urate excretion**, raising serum urate and provoking gout. Only **high doses** are uricosuric. Thiazides, loop diuretics, niacin and cyclosporine act similarly.

drug.name: Aspirin (low dose)
drug.how: Acetylates COX-1 and COX-2; at low dose it competes for tubular urate secretion, reducing excretion
drug.use: Secondary prevention of coronary and cerebrovascular disease; higher doses for analgesia and inflammation
drug.watch: Raised urate and gout at low dose; gastric ulcer and bleeding; Reye syndrome in children; tinnitus in overdose

idea.rule: Drugs that compete for urate secretion raise serum urate.
also: Lactate and ketoacids (alcohol, fasting) compete the same way

stem: A 57-year-old man with chronic tophaceous gout takes a daily medicine to prevent attacks. He is given a course of penicillin for cellulitis. Over the next days his blood penicillin levels stay higher and last longer than expected, though his renal function is normal.
oneliner: 57M + chronic gout on a daily preventive drug + penicillin for cellulitis + penicillin levels higher and longer than expected + normal renal function → which gout drug explains it?
ask: Which gout drug most likely explains the prolonged penicillin levels?

whyNot.B: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor; it **lowers urate production** and does not block tubular **penicillin secretion**
whyNot.C: A tubulin binder with **no effect** on renal organic acid secretion
whyNot.D: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor; it acts on **urate production**, not renal **penicillin secretion**
whyNot.E: An NSAID used for **acute flares**, not daily prevention, with no important effect on **penicillin levels**

why: **Probenecid** is a uricosuric that blocks **organic acid transport in the proximal tubule (URAT1 and OAT)**. It also blocks the tubular **secretion of penicillin**, so penicillin levels rise and last longer, a property sometimes used deliberately.

drug.name: Probenecid
drug.class: Uricosuric (URAT1 and organic acid transport inhibitor)
drug.how: Blocks URAT1 and organic anion transporters in the proximal tubule, increasing urate excretion and reducing penicillin secretion
drug.use: Chronic gout from underexcretion; adjunct to prolong penicillin levels
drug.watch: Raised levels of penicillins; uric acid stones; do not start during an acute flare

idea.rule: Probenecid blocks tubular secretion of weak organic acids, including penicillins.
also: Also raises levels of cephalosporins, methotrexate and ketorolac
Once given with penicillin or cefoxitin for gonorrhea
Use with salicylates blunts its uricosuric effect
Avoid in overproducers and kidney stones
